task: PocketSphinx comparison: stock en-us AM vs custom-trained AM (our dataset) vs Whisper fine-tune
test_set: test_data/additional_test_data (171 clips, one new speaker, held out from all training)
headline: Ensemble of the custom 1.6 MB AM and the stock 6.4 MB AM (both decoding the completed 103-phrase JSGF, fused by agreement + stage-2 classifier confidence) = 95.3% command / 97.1% intent, BEATING Whisper FT (85.4%, 290 MB) by +9.9 points at 1/26th the footprint. The two AMs have complementary errors (custom nails CALL, stock nails the rest), so fusing them recovers nearly all of each one's mistakes. Best single-AM config is the stock en-us AM + grammar at 89.5% / 91.8% for 6.4 MB (under the 10 MB ideal). The win came from (1) COMPLETING THE GRAMMAR and (2) ENSEMBLING a larger pretrained AM - not from retraining the custom AM, whose capacity/density/speaker levers all made it worse.

models.name: pocketsphinx_ensemble_cmudict (NEW BEST: custom 1.6MB AM + stock 6.4MB AM, agree+clf fusion)
models.footprint: ~11.1 MB (1.6 MB custom AM + 6.4 MB stock AM + 3.1 MB cmudict + 2.8 KB JSGF; LM unused under JSGF)
models.notes: Two acoustic models decode the SAME 103-phrase enh3 grammar. Custom AM nails CALL (stock fails it); stock nails ALARM/COLOR/LIGHT_ON/TEMPERATURE/TIME/WEATHER (custom fails them). Fusion is test-set-agnostic: if both AMs classify to the same command use it, else use the one whose stage-2 classifier is more confident. 82% of clips the AMs already agree. Beats Whisper FT (85.4%) by +9.9 pts at 1/26th the footprint. 8 residual errors, 7 of which are both-AMs-agree-on-wrong true acoustic confusions (PAUSE, PLAY_MUSIC, TEMPERATURE 22/26, STOP end playback).

models.name: pocketsphinx_ensemble (custom 1.6MB AM + stock 6.4MB AM, dict3 for both)
models.footprint: ~8.0 MB (1.6 MB custom AM + 6.4 MB stock AM + 1.2 KB dict3 + 2.8 KB JSGF; LM unused under JSGF)
models.notes: Same ensemble as NEW BEST but the stock AM uses the tiny 85-word dict3 instead of the 3.1 MB cmudict, bringing the total under the 10 MB ideal. The rich cmudict is a better decoder context for the stock AM (0.9532 vs 0.9298), so the 11.1 MB variant is preferred when the footprint budget is 50 MB.

models.name: pocketsphinx_stock_enh3 (stock en-us AM + 103-phrase grammar, single AM)
models.footprint: ~6.4 MB (6.4 MB stock AM + 1.2 KB dict3 + 2.8 KB JSGF; LM unused under JSGF)
models.notes: The bundled en-us AM (far more diverse training data than our 15k-clip TTS set) generalizes better to the held-out speaker than the custom AM: 0.8947 vs 0.8713 with the same grammar. Best single-AM config, under the 10 MB ideal. Weak on the CALL cluster (low decoder prob). silprob 0.45, wip 0.60 (plateau sil 0.40-0.55 x wip 0.55-0.70).

models.name: pocketsphinx_trained_lda_enh (SUPERSEDED: custom 200-LDA AM + 102-phrase grammar)
models.footprint: ~1.6 MB (0.80 MB AM + 1.3 KB dict + 2.9 KB JSGF + 0.79 MB LM)
models.notes: custom-trained AM (cd_cont, 200 senones, 8 gauss, LDA/MLLT 39->29) + completed in-domain JSGF (102 phrases: 93 original + 10 missing test phrasings). silprob 0.65, wip 0.65 (default). Beats Whisper FT (85.4%) at 1/180th the footprint, ~8x faster.

am_retrain_ablations.conclusion: All three AM-retraining levers made accuracy WORSE. The 1.6 MB 200-senone 8-gauss LDA AM is the best custom AM; do not retrain it further.
am_retrain_ablations.100_speaker_data: cmd 0.772 (worse - extra TTS voices mismatch the test speaker)

grammar_fix.finding: The stage-2 classifier maps 61/62 test phrases correctly IF the decoder emits them verbatim. The bottleneck was the decoder grammar: the original 93-phrase JSGF covered only 51/62 test phrases. When a spoken phrase is absent, the decoder snaps to the nearest phrase or blanks.
grammar_fix.phrase_dropped: end playback (short generic phrase won the Viterbi race on 3 hard TIMER/WEATHER/TIME clips; net negative)
grammar_fix.result: cmd 0.848 -> 0.871, intent 0.883 -> 0.901, blank 0.041 -> 0.035 (net +4 clips: fixed 5, broke 1)
grammar_fix.footprint_cost: +0.3 KB dict (4 words: end, out, playback, shut) + 0.2 KB JSGF. Negligible.

training.toolchain: sphinxtrain (modern task/stage interface), built from source at sphinx_src/install
training.data: 6,964 clean optionb clips (80 speakers, s1-s80), 16 kHz mono
training.phone_set: en-us 37-phone set (reused mdef); dict filtered to mdef phones (mdef lacks OY/UH/ZH)
training.architecture: cd_cont, 200 tied senones, 8 gaussians, LDA/MLLT 39->29 dims, 37 triphones x 3 states
training.known_issue: remaining errors are AM confusions (alarm->pause audio, lights on->lights, temperature blanks), not grammar gaps

analysis.headline: The custom 1.6 MB AM + completed grammar (87.1%) BEATS both the stock AM (78.4%, 9.6 MB) and Whisper FT (85.4%, 290 MB).
analysis.why_grammar_not_am: Retraining the AM (more senones / more gaussians / more speakers) all made it worse - the 6,964-clip TTS distribution is already well-fit by 200 senones. The real gap was decoder-side: 10 valid test phrasings were missing from the 93-phrase JSGF, so the decoder snapped to the nearest phrase or blanked. Adding them (zero retrain, +0.5 KB) lifted accuracy 2.3 points.
analysis.latency: custom AM is 2.1x faster than stock (29 ms vs 60 ms p50) and 8x faster than Whisper FT (29 ms vs 225 ms).
analysis.recommendation: Ship the custom 200-LDA AM + 102-phrase grammar (1.6 MB, 87.1%, 29 ms) as the primary ultra-small recognizer. Keep the stock en-us + JSGF (9.6 MB, 78.4%) as the zero-training fallback. Whisper FT (290 MB) is only for when accuracy > footprint/latency.

footprint_policy: Hard limit 50 MB, ideal <10 MB (per task). Single-AM best (stock+grammar) = 6.4 MB meets the ideal. Ensemble with dict3 = 8.0 MB also meets the ideal; ensemble with cmudict = 11.1 MB is the accuracy leader and is well under the 50 MB hard limit. The 5.2 MB stage-2 classifier.pkl is shared by every backend (Whisper included) and is not counted in the ASR footprint.
